### Chapter Eighteen.

## *On the Chemical Alphabet.*

#### *Namely, how the characters, signs, and words of the ancient philosophers are to be understood and interpreted.*

1. In the preceding chapters, I have written clearly and expressly enough—as far as God has permitted me—concerning the <term>First Matter</term> <note>Materia prima: the primitive, formless base of all reality</note>, the <term>Solvent</term> <note>Menstruum: a substance used to dissolve or extract solids, named after the lunar cycle</note>, and the Universal Medicine; likewise concerning the *Magical* elements or keys. However, since this might prove somewhat difficult for beginning students, seeing as the philosophical style is still unknown to them, and since I intend nothing else but to serve all faithful and honest Sons of the Art, I have found it highly necessary to begin from a humble and simple understanding. I have therefore decided to attach a Chemical Alphabet and certain new characters which truly show the property of the things designated. Therefore, the fair lover of the arts will take unique care in examining this Alphabet and the attached new characters, for from there the first light arises.

2. The Philosophers have compared their matter, or solvent, to the sharpest vinegar, and likewise to vitriol or saltpeter, because this contains all the qualities which are attributed to the First Matter by the philosophers; for it is found to be moist and dry, cold and hot, light and heavy, according to how we wish to have it. Now, <term>Mercury</term> <note>Mercurius: here referring to the philosophical principle of fluidity and transformation rather than just common quicksilver</note> similarly possesses this property, and it is clear that the <term>Philosophers' Stone</term> cannot be made without it; for that reason, the Sages do not act unjustly when they call their Matter "Mercury."

3. But as for the fact that many desire to attain their salvation <note>meaning their success in the work</note> from cold <term>Saturn</term> <note>The alchemical name for Lead, associated with the planet Saturn and the beginning of the transformation process</note>, since the <term>Great Work</term> <note>Opus Magnum: the process of creating the Philosophers' Stone</note> is ascribed to it, that very thing is so...

15. Whoever now wishes to know the correct name and character of the **First Matter** <note>materia prima; the fundamental starting material of the Great Work</note>, let him know that from the combination of figures, syllables result, and from these truly a significant word, or a universal character, which I have sketched above in the title. However, it is not contained in such a simple, despicable, or contrary form as the philosophers have made it; nevertheless, it is visibly findable therein, and can be constructed from there very simply. This is the reason why I wished to record only these few characters; these are like little lights which ought to lead you to the true light of knowledge. And although I intended to reveal something greater here, I am indeed restrained from this by the shortness of time, especially since it is clear to me that similar characters are not to be found in the printing shops, and to engrave or cast such things would take too long, and thus the work would be delayed, preventing this New Light from rising at these present Fairs <note>likely referring to the book fairs where such manuscripts were sold</note>, which I would take poorly.

16. Since the time has now arrived in which I wish to more willingly serve mankind through my talent during these few remaining years of my life, I must therefore break off my thread of discourse. In the meantime, I highly recommend to you this <term>Chemical Alphabet<note>original: "Alphabetum Chymicum"; likely a symbolic or coded system of alchemical notation</note></term>; with the promise that, should God deign to grant me grace, I shall attach those few remaining new figures at the first opportunity. Indeed, for this reason, I must expect to suffer detraction from both the virtuous and the wicked alike. To the wise and virtuous, it is displeasing that I have written so clearly; the wicked, however, whom the Almighty does not favor, will think I have spoken too obscurely on the matter, or will hold other sinister opinions regarding it. Although the potential offense to those virtuous men already experienced in the Art <note>The "Art" refers to Alchemy or the Hermetic sciences</note> might rightly deter me, I nevertheless feel compassion for those other virtuous but unlearned men and sincere Lovers of the Art, to whom I would gladly communicate my experience. I pity those who are worn out and preoccupied by so many <term>cacochymical</term> <note>From the Greek 'kakochymos,' meaning 'bad juice' or 'ill-humored'; here referring to books containing corrupt or false chemical theories</note> books, laboring in vain.

2. Therefore, know first that all things are formed and made into such similar bodies out of three essences, through astral impression and elemental operation. Elements are found in metals, and non-metals in elements; for the seed of metals is not so far removed as certain "know-it-alls" have imagined. And although the elements must cooperate in the formation of any body, they are not the <term>materia prima</term> <note>The "First Matter" or the primordial, formless substance required to create the Philosopher's Stone</note> of the philosophers, or that <term>astral seed</term> <note>The celestial or spiritual influence that gives life and form to matter</note>; rather, they are the cause of generation and corruption, and the corruption of one is the generation of another.

3. The ancient philosophers believe that every thing was created out of hate or love—that is, out of <term>sympathy and antipathy</term>—as if from two mutually opposing qualities of the elements, which carry out this operation through celestial influence and special astral impression, etc. Now, the elements are incorporated within metals and minerals, and therefore they also possess the same qualities as the elements. There are only two contrary qualities through which whatever exists is generated and born: Fire is hot and dry, its contrary is the cold, moist element of Water; Air is moist and hot, its contrary is the dry, cold Earth. And since no body can be found outside of those four elements, and the elements are incorporated in all things, a certain contrariety arises within every element.

considered. For these reasons, all things beneath the sphere of the moon are perishable and destructible. Because as long as two contraries persist within a single subject, an unceasing struggle occurs, until at last one part receives aid from its external element; for then the opposing part must immediately withdraw and yield the victory to the stronger. From this arises a certain corruption, or a separation of the entire substance, so that a new form—which was generated through that corruption—lies before our eyes.

4. The elements of metals are their *three primordial* matrices: Mercury, Sulphur, and Salt. <note>These are the 'Tria Prima' of Paracelsian alchemy, representing the spirit, soul, and body of matter.</note> These are like contraries in continuous battle and enmity; because Mercury, as an aerial spirit, carries on a hostility against Salt, which represents the earth; and hot Sulphur, like fire, is the enemy of water—namely, it is contrary to the humidity of Mercury. For this [Mercury] is the "water" of metals and represents two elements, both air and water. These aforementioned three matrices, or metallic elements, have their nourishment from our material, visible, and tangible elements. They struggle within their mortal home until a fixed time, until one element, through external assistance, becomes too strong for the other and suppresses it, since no help is given to the weaker from its own kind. 

And just as a human being, when one element dominates within him, falls into a serious infirmity—and first his fat (like sulphur) fails, and afterwards his flesh and blood also fail and he is forced to die, unless we provide the necessary restoration to the suffering or predominant element and establish a certain suitable harmony anew—therefore, it is necessary for a physician to know which principle or element is acting in the patient and which is suffering. Just as it happens now in the microcosm <note>The human body, viewed as a miniature reflection of the universe.</note>, so it also occurs in metals and minerals, which, through the strengthening of one or another element, suppress and suffocate the contrary element, so that corruption and separation must follow from this.

I will not pass over the relationship of both that Saturn <note>In alchemy, Saturn usually refers to the metal Lead or a specific cold, heavy state of matter</note> and Mercury here; therefore, lend your ears solely to my teaching. You have heard above that from the Moon <note>Silver</note>, and similarly from that cold Saturn of the Ram <note>Aries; likely referring to a specific astrological timing or a grade of antimony/lead</note>, a certain Mercury can be made, and that this serves specifically for the Work of the Wise <term>Opus sapientum: the Great Work of alchemy</term>; *Secondly*, that from the ore of Venus <note>Copper</note> it is also possible to produce a certain Solar Mercury, which is endowed with solar sulfur, which is why I baptized it in that same place the "Mercury of the Sun," since it is to be employed for the generation of Gold. *Thirdly*, that I, notwithstanding this, have already used the Mercury of Saturn for the destruction of gold; therefore, regarding this doubt, I say that even the Red Mercury can be employed in the White Lunar Tincture with great and better advantage. And just as we are not able to move from one extreme to another without a middle point, in no other way can we arrive at any Red Tincture unless the White has been obtained first; thus the benevolent reader may now resolve his own scruple and remember that I have written here not concerning the "Most General Universal," but only concerning the "Simple Universal."

24. The Most General Universal is produced from a double Mercury, as I related above, and is animated and fermented with solar sulfur, and fixed with the enduring salt of gold; it is also further augmented unto infinity through two other sulfurs, both in quantity and quality. The quality, like life, is fed by sulfur; the quantity is increased by the aforementioned Mercury, which carries with it not only the character and faculty of the property of Venus, but also the nature of the cold mineral Saturn. Therefore, it is likened to a double Mercury and is called *doubled* Mercury, to which all qualities are appropriated; for it has the quality of Venus by reason of the hot sulfur, but coldness on the part of Saturn. *Let the fair and emulous Lover of the Art* <note>original: "Candidus æmulúſque artis Amator"</note> dismiss every doubt, I pray, and place faith in my experience in truth. You may do whatever you wish, yet you will be able to accuse me of no lie, because I have not begged this from other books to procure a more famous name for myself in some way; but through the labor of my own hands I have risked—

<summary>The author explains the synthesis of a "doubled Mercury" by combining the properties of Saturn (cold) and Venus (heat), emphasizing that the White Tincture must precede the Red. He asserts his authority based on practical laboratory experience rather than merely citing other texts.</summary>

# A PLAIN RECAPITULATION.

I have reflected, and afterwards I understood that which I ought to have known before.

25. To the sincere *lover of the art* <note>original: "technophilo"; one who loves the technical mastery of alchemy</note> happens the explanation of the fundamental mystery of the Sages, which I indeed described above, but now, in this final reaping of the gleanings, I have embraced as succinctly as possible, so that by reading this repetition frequently, you might reiterate it until you are taught all things internally and externally. And since I am not unaware that this *Commentary* of mine cannot be refuted, it will be bought up in all places, partly out of fear and partly out of hatred and envy, so that it will reach the hands of only a few; I, however, shall gather my own from this and know what I have done, and what I am yet to do in the future.

26. Meanwhile, I wish my repetition to be finished here, regarding the two *Magical* elements, the Solvent <note>original: "Menstrui"; a liquid solvent used in alchemy to dissolve solids</note> or the *doubled* Mercury, and I shall abstain from treating the medicine which consists in the monarchy of minerals. Therefore, receive with a grateful heart these first fruits of my labor with the *Magical* elements, with the Solvent and the Universal Medicine, and with the First Matter <note>original: "Materia Prima"; the primitive, formless base of all matter</note>, through which any metal can be reduced into its *three* principles, and true Potable Gold <note>original: "aurum Potabile"; gold refined into a liquid drinkable form, believed to be a sovereign remedy</note> ought to be made. The first matter has been outlined for you in express words, just as both elements or the fiery key <note>original: "ignea clavis"</note> have been clearly, even transparently, demonstrated to the eye, so that I believe you will not desire anything more lucid.

27. May the Eternal, merciful Creator <note>original: "Conditor"</note> of heaven and earth, the first and the last, who holds the key of Olympus and the Underworld <note>original: "Olympi & Orci"; referring to the heights of heaven and the depths of the grave</note>, deign to illuminate the minds and talents of the worthy and humble, and so shut and seal the understanding and will of the impious, the proud, and the greedy, so that no evil may come from this my faithful and sincere intention, but that every good ought to be practiced by it, for the honor and praise of His Holy name, the benefit of our neighbor, and the health and blessedness of our own souls. Amen.

# A PLAIN RECAPITULATION.

# MEMORIAL
### To the
# READER.

<margin>1.</margin>
Kind Reader, since in my preceding writings I have made one or two obligations which might yield profit and utility to the gracious reader, and furthermore since I have promised to allow the true, irreducible <term>Potable Gold<note>Latin: Aurum Potabile. A legendary alchemical medicine consisting of gold dissolved or suspended in a liquid form, believed to be a universal cure.</note></term> to be prepared and perfected so that those who require this as a <term>Universal Medicine<note>Latin: Universali Medicina. A "panacea" or cure-all sought by alchemists to heal all bodily ailments and prolong life.</note></term> might be able to seek and obtain it: And since I also, for singular and weighty reasons, am intended to fix my residence at a certain place; meanwhile, however, so that I may keep my obligation and promises made by my word uninjured, I ought by right to inform the honest reader where I am to be sought out. For in the absence of this information, the obligation and promises grow obsolete and take on the appearance of mere boasting. Therefore, let the fair reader know that, although I shall not be found at <term>Cologne<note>Latin: Colonia Agrippina. A major center for trade and alchemy in the early modern period.</note></term>, where I have stayed for a long enough time, instruction regarding my presence may nevertheless be had there from Jacob Janus (whose name is very well known in the courier's office—commonly called the Post and Counting House—and otherwise to many lovers of the arts in various places). The reason, however, why I wish to remain unknown is that I have determined to give myself over to quiet; meanwhile, at Cologne, with the aforementioned Jacob, the <term>Drinkable Gold<note>Latin: Aurum Poculentum.</note></term> may be obtained, which is fashioned from the <term>blood of the true Lion<note>Latin: Leonis sanguine. An alchemical metaphor; the "Lion" often refers to antimony or a specific state of gold/mercury during the transmutation process.</note></term>.

->MEMORANDUM TO THE READER.<-

*...or the soul of the Sun <note>original: "anima Solis"; in alchemy, this refers to the essential sulfur or "soul" of gold</note> is at hand, it must be resolved into oil in a friendly manner, without noise or scorching, by that familiar Philosophical Spirit. Hence, by means of the spirit of wine <note>alcohol</note>, Potable Gold <note>original: "Aurum Potabile"; a legendary medicinal liquid gold</note> is made; otherwise, and even without it, a tincture is produced through Vulcan <note>the god of fire, representing alchemical heat</note>. In that case, however, the Salt of gold must be present, which can easily be obtained from a certain dead body from which the soul has departed; so that, besides the principles, a certain fourth thing may yet be seen, which I baptize as the "earthly curse" and "sinning matter," or the receptacle of its own evil and of another's good.*

*Wherever now, by the help of such a separation, the tincture is extracted from the Solar sulfur by the Universal Solvent <note>original: "Universale Menstruum"; the "Alkahest" or substance capable of dissolving all others</note>, there, in all eternity, no reduction into the former shape is to be hoped for or effected. Because a malleable metallic body must have its hardness and malleability from its Salt, but here there is only the mere soul and spirit of Hermes <note>referring to Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy</note>. Therefore, our solution, or our potable gold, must be called true and irreducible, which I teach here in the truth of the matter. For that reason, let the fair-minded Reader trust me, and let him not doubt that a certain tincture can be obtained through this.*

3. *But restore to that glorified fiery soul its own clarified body and Salt, and lead back this animated spirit through the salt into coagulation; thus the spiritual is made corporeal. You, indeed, shall see what the Most High is going to give you, if you await the time with patience and foresight. To Him alone shall you attribute the honor, because I am nothing more than a certain voice crying in the wilderness, which proclaims to you the light of Wisdom, Wealth, and Health to be attained; for the light is that Alpha and Omega, the prow and the stern <note>the beginning and the end</note> of all things.*

<summary>The author describes the extraction of the "soul of gold" to create a true Potable Gold and warns that once the tincture is separated from its metallic salt, it cannot be returned to its original metallic form. He emphasizes that the process requires patience and divine favor to achieve the ultimate goals of wisdom and health.</summary>

# The Correctness of the Work.

->*As much as is known up until now.*<-

No large or serious errors are present; however, very small ones (namely through the transposition or change of a single letter) have crept in, and these are very few indeed. Therefore, one should read:

**Page 7, line 18:** *Mecœnati* <note>original: "Mecœnati"</note> with the *œ* diphthong in the middle, instead of *Mæcenati*. <note>A reference to Gaius Maecenas, the famous Roman patron of the arts; the author is correcting the Latin spelling of the name.</note>
**P. 12, verse 4:** *Nuntius* <note>Messenger</note>, instead of *Muntius* with an *M*, by an error of the typesetter; and likewise in the same place, *dicitur* <note>it is said</note>, instead of *diciter*.
**P. 27, verse 3:** *Hesperios* <note>Westerners</note>, instead of *Hesperidos*, but only in some copies.
**P. 55, third to last line:** *fillos*, in place of *fales*, for the sake of the poetry. <note>Likely a correction to maintain the meter or rhythm of a verse.</note>
Also in the same place, second to last line: *Parœmiographo* <note>Writer of proverbs</note>, with the *œ* diphthong, instead of *Paræmiographo* with the *æ* diphthong.
**p. 66, l. 11:** *audite* <note>hear/listen</note>, instead of *audire* <note>to hear</note>, because the sense will be better connected this way.
**p. 80, verse 2:** *nunc* <note>now</note>, instead of *nnnc*, with three *n*s.
**p. 82, verse 11:** *defluxit* <note>flowed down</note>, instead of *distabuit* <note>melted away</note> (for the sake of the <term>syllabic quantity</term> <note>the length of vowels in Latin poetry</note> and the improvement of the meaning), and this is in only a few copies.
**p. 116, l. 25:** *mundum* <note>world</note>, instead of *mundnm*, with one *u*.
**p. 125, l. 10:** *conopeis* <note>mosquito nets/canopies</note>, without the *œ* diphthong, instead of *conopæis* with it; also in very few copies.
**p. 128, l. 18:** *prudentiâ* <note>with prudence</note>, instead of *prudenti*, by the carelessness of the typesetter, though in very few copies.
**p. 157, l. 21:** *Sibyllæ* <note>of the Sibyl</note>, instead of *Sibullæ*, but in most copies.
**p. 216, l. 25:** *catenâ* <note>with a chain</note>, instead of *cathenâ*, with the aspiration <note>the addition of the 'h'</note>.
**p. 281, verse 2 or line 8:** *Qui* <note>Who</note>, instead of *Qui⁷*, with the little mark and the <term>cipher</term> <note>number</note> 7; but only in certain copies; an error of the typesetter.
**p. 291, l. 5:** *itineris sui* <note>of his journey</note>, instead of *suis*: almost the greatest fault that I know to be present.
**p. 63:** read *tato*, instead of *de*, the last syllable or indicative tail; by the carelessness and error of the typesetter.
**finally p. 67, l. 1:** *Saturnos duos* <note>two Saturns</note>, instead of *Saturnus duos*; truly the greatest error that is present, etc.
